faqs.question: How do I register for online or mobile banking?
alternate_questions: How to sign up for internet banking
Enable app access for my account
faqs.answer: You can usually register through your bank's website or app using your account number or card details, along with identity verification, often via an SMS or email code. Some banks require an initial branch visit or an activation code by mail for extra security before online access is fully enabled.

faqs.question: I forgot my online banking password, what do I do?
alternate_questions: Can't log in to online banking
faqs.answer: Use the 'Forgot Password' option on the login page, which usually verifies your identity through your registered phone number, email, or security questions before letting you set a new password. If that doesn't work, contact your bank's support line or visit a branch with identification.

faqs.question: Is online banking safe?
alternate_questions: Is it safe to use the banking app?
Can my account be hacked through the app?
faqs.answer: Bank apps and websites use encryption and multiple layers of security, such as passwords, one-time codes and sometimes biometrics, making them generally safe when used carefully. Risks mostly come from user behavior, like weak passwords, public Wi-Fi, or falling for phishing scams, rather than the platform itself. Always use official apps and links.

faqs.question: My banking app isn't working, what should I do?
faqs.answer: First try closing and reopening the app, checking your internet connection, and updating the app to the latest version. If the problem continues, restart your device, or reinstall the app. If it still fails, it may be a temporary outage on the bank's side, so check their status page or contact support.

faqs.question: What is two-factor authentication (2FA) in banking?
alternate_questions: Why do I need a code to log in?
faqs.answer: Two-factor authentication adds a second layer of security beyond your password, usually a one-time code (OTP) sent by SMS or generated by an app, or a biometric check like a fingerprint. It ensures that even if someone learns your password, they still can't access your account without the second factor.

faqs.question: Can I use online banking on multiple devices?
alternate_questions: Log in to banking app on two phones
Use online banking on a new phone
Switch banking app to new device
faqs.answer: Most banks allow login from multiple devices, though some may require re-verification when logging in from a new device for security. If you get a new phone, you'll typically need to log in again and complete identity verification to link the app to that device.

faqs.question: How do I get e-statements or turn off paper statements?
faqs.answer: You can usually enable e-statements and disable paper mail in your account settings within the app or online banking, or by contacting customer service. E-statements are typically available for download as PDFs each statement cycle and are often sent by email as well.

faqs.question: What can I do with mobile banking besides checking balances?
alternate_questions: What can the mobile app do?
Things I can do online with my bank
faqs.answer: Beyond checking balances, most apps let you transfer money, pay bills, deposit checks by photo, block or manage cards, apply for loans or cards, set up alerts, view statements, and message customer support. Available features vary by bank, so check your app's menu.

faqs.question: How do I set up transaction alerts?
faqs.answer: Alert settings are usually found in your app or online banking under notifications or alerts, where you can choose to be notified by SMS, email or push notification for transactions, low balance, or login attempts. Enabling these helps you spot unauthorized activity quickly.

faqs.question: How do I log out of online banking on another device?
alternate_questions: Sign out of banking app remotely
Remove an old device from banking
faqs.answer: Open your bank's security or device-management settings and choose the option to sign out of all sessions or remove the device. If you lost the phone or suspect unauthorized access, change your password and contact the bank immediately through an official channel.

faqs.question: What should I do if I did not receive my banking OTP?
faqs.answer: Check that your registered phone has signal, wait briefly, and request a new code only through the official app or website. Do not share any OTP with anyone. If codes repeatedly fail to arrive, confirm your contact details with the bank using its official support channel.
